Chippewas of Rama First Nation

The Chippewas of Rama First Nation’s own publications connect community history with the Chippewa Tri-Council and the Mnjikaning fish-weir landscape. A separate school account describes how education and language learning are organized within Rama.

01

History told by the community

Rama’s public history identifies its links with the Chippewas of Beausoleil and Georgina Island through the Chippewa Tri-Council. It recounts displacement through the Coldwater Narrows experiment and rebuilding at Rama. The page also describes a community archive made public in 2018 and attributes accounts of the Mnjikaning fish weirs to Elders. These relationships do not make the three First Nations one interchangeable government.

Read the sources [1] Chippewas of Rama First Nation

02

A purpose-built school and language learning

Rama’s account of Mnjikaning Kendaaswin Elementary School dates its opening to 1998 and describes a purpose-built place for community education. Its stated approach combines curriculum learning with Ojibwe language and cultural knowledge, supported by community educational bodies. This describes the institution’s published approach; it does not establish uniform experiences or measured outcomes for every student.
